explanation: In Egypt, the OK hand sign (thumb and index finger forming a circle) is not universally understood as positive; it can be interpreted as a threat or a vulgar gesture implying 'you are zero' or 'I will harm you,' especially in informal or tense settings. While younger, globally connected Egyptians may recognize its Western meaning, older or more traditional individuals may find it offensive.
local_tip: Avoid using the OK hand sign entirely in Egypt; instead, use a thumbs-up or a verbal affirmation like 'tayyib' (okay) to convey agreement.
regional_note: In rural areas and among older generations, the sign is more likely to be seen as rude or threatening, whereas in urban, cosmopolitan Cairo it may be tolerated among youth.

also_check.note: Considered a highly offensive gesture equivalent to an obscene insult.
